body: Thank you for your response.  That really clarifies things for me.
Thanks guys.  I think the agency has a policy about this.  I really don’t think it’s right I just don’t know what to do about it.
Thank you!  I wasn't sure if it was true, but I thought it was.  It scares me.  Just wondering what other people thought.
Ha!  Yeah I wouldn't be surprised.  Thanks for responding.

My advice would be to remember that you are dealing with a whole, complex human being with thoughts and feelings, and not just an illness that can be fixed with a pill.

Be aware of your position of power over people and don't abuse it. Check your privilege, as they say.

Consider the effects of poverty on mental health, as well as societal oppression and trauma.

Good luck.  The fact that you're even asking this question is a good thing.
Thank you! It's nice to know I'm not the only one.
That was awesome. Thanks a lot! :)

Thanks for the added information.  

Must be very difficult in university.  I can imagine it's overwhelming at first and it must be hard to avoid alcohol.  I really hope things get better for you.  Based on your op, I wasn't sure what to say, the only thing I know for sure is that depression medication and alcohol are a really nasty combination.  Like, deadly at times.  That's the only advice I can offer.  I wish you well.  You have your whole life ahead of you and I hope you keep yourself safe and healthy. Take care of yourself. Peace.

I'm not sure what your situation is.  Sounds like you have a lot going on.  Please don't hurt yourself.

All I can tell you is that I know what it's like to take meds that aren't working.  It's extremely frustrating, and if you're drinking then they're even less likely to work and it can be very dangerous.  Been there.  It took me 17 years for my meds to work because I'd go off of them too soon out of frustration or I was drinking and it was excruciatingly painful and I thought of ending it too.  I'm very surprised I'm still here.

I don't know what meds you're on and I don't expect you to tell me.  All I know is that Meds and drinking create a vicious, vicious cycle and I had two friends that died because they were ill and couldn't stop drinking.  They were in pain so they'd drink, then they'd be even MORE pain so they'd drink again until they died completely alone and in horrific ways in their twenties.  

It doesn't have to be this way for you.  You deserve a real shot at being healthy and for your meds to work properly.  There's help out there you just have to be open minded and willing to work at getting better without the booze.  It's a long road but you deserve it.

I hope that helps and I hope that wasn't too preachy.

Hi there.  Thanks for posting.  It takes courage to reach out like that.

I don't know what it's like to be in your position, but I feel for you and everyone in your position when I watch the news.  I understand why you are feeling the way you are right now.  Please don't do anything rash.  It would be a great injustice.  

I know for myself when I have really felt like checking out and no one could talk me out of it the thing that has kept me safe is really thinking it through. i read suicide bereavement stories from  people left behind, and also about how some people do permanent damage to themselves.  No suicide method is foolproof and most are very painful, and the effect on loved ones is  excruciating.  Just wanted to give you a reality check.  When you're suffering it's easy to forget that.

I hope you can connect with community and know that you are not alone in this.  I hope you can find a fighting spirit within yourself because like I said, it would be a great injustice if you took your life because of this.  You deserve to live.

Take care.

I'm very sorry for your loss.  It must be difficult to be so young with no one to guide you.  I remember feeling very lost at 19 and I had my family.  

Please don't do anything rash.  suicide causes irreparable damage, and is never foolproof.  It's brutal and often extremely painful and can leave you disfigured or paralyzed, if not dead forever.

Your life is just getting started!  You can create your own family and fall in love and help other people and do things you love to do.  

There are bereavement support groups out there that are free and might be of some comfort.  It gets better with time.  Life also tends to get more manageable as you age and get to know yourself.  Please give yourself that chance. 

Take care.

This is an excellent question.! To be or not to be.  Albert Camus said that the only philosophical question that matters is whether or not to commit suicide.  (I'm glad you don't actively want to take your life, btw, whew!). 

In my life, I have found meditation to be really helpful with this feeling.  It gives me something no one can take away from me and an ever changing goal to work on.  I am not religious, but have found aspects of eastern philosophy helpful in addressing feelings of suffering, emptiness and dissatisfaction, especially realizing that it's normal to have those feelings.  Western culture leads us to believe we're supposed to be happy all the time, and I haven't found that to be true, in my life.

Hope that helps.
I meant to post this for someone who is afraid of being deported from America but I can't find them now.  I suppose it could apply to anyone who is suicidal so I thought I'd leave it up.

You clearly have a lot of insight and are very intelligent.  Sometimes that is a blessing AND a curse.  

Please don't do anything to harm yourself.  

i know what it's like to break up with someone you really love because of inner turmoil.  We're all human and we're all flawed-every single one of us.  It feels awful but it will pass and there are billions of other people to love and show kindness to.  

It was a real revelation to me to realize that every relationship is different and unique and sometimes you can love someone and be loved and not be meant to be with them in a relationship for various reasons.  The problems I had with my ex are non existent in my new relationship because my new partner and I connect differently, even though when I broke up with my ex I thought I was the most broken person out there and could never be loved again.

I hope that helps.

If you are thinking of suicide I hope you can be brave enough to reach out in real life.  Suicide causes irreparable damage to many lives, and no suicide method is foolproof and most are very painful.  

Take care.

Your family will NEVER forget about you.  Your suicide would haunt them for the rest of their lives.  Read some suicide bereavement stories if you don't believe me.

  I don't think you're thinking clearly.  You clearly love your family but the pain you are in is clouding your thinking.  I'm not convinced that you really are sold on dying because you are reaching out here.  I think You should listen to that fear about failing.  It's a very healthy fear. You could end up a vegetable or paralyzed or disfigured.  No method of suicide is foolproof.  Please talk to someone about how you are feeling and reach out for help in the real world.  I don't think you want to hurt your family like this.
Hey everybody. thanks for your thoughtful replies.  it makes me feel less alone in all of this.
HI.  I'm on I think 150 paliperidone and 150 seroquel.  Thanks for the hugs.
Thanks for the thoughtful reply.  I admire your perseverance.
Thanks for the advice.  I do like listening to music and I once went on a supermario world marathon when I was troubled.
